## Paper

Governing the Commons

## World

resource_island

## Institution

Property rights and reputation governance.

## Agent type

Common-pool resource users / learning agents.

## Theoretical benchmark

Governance works through boundaries, monitoring, graduated sanctions, and local rule fit.

## Learning setup

Spatial resource world with property claims, reputation bonuses, trading, and contested resources.

## Metrics

Property opportunity counts, property violations, trade counts, welfare, sustainability, survival, inequality.

## Main result

The book documents cases where self-organized common-pool institutions can govern resources through boundaries, monitoring, sanctions, and locally adapted rules. Use it as governance-design framing, not as evidence that this repo's simple hooks reproduce real institutional richness.

## What they prove

Not a formal proof for this repo's purposes. It supplies empirically grounded design principles and governance mechanisms that Resource Island can only approximate.

## What they only simulate

Not applicable for this card's thesis use: it is book-level institutional analysis and case-based evidence, not a simulation benchmark.

## What they do NOT test

Artificial learning agents, neural/MARL policies, explicit activation-threshold diagnostics, and the simplified property/reputation hooks used by Resource Island.

## What we need to reproduce

Property/reputation mechanisms must have activation diagnostics before welfare differences are interpreted.

## How our project differs

The book studies real common-pool institutions. The repo tests narrow institutional hooks and must not claim full Ostrom governance from simple counters.

## Implementation obligations

Property claim counter; non-owner opportunity counter; violation counter; reputation/trade counter; activation thresholds; v1 contested layouts.

## Metrics to compare in our repo

Resource Island v1 property opportunities, violations, and trade diagnostics; outputs/resource_island_v1_full.

## Failure modes to audit

Zero violations interpreted as success when no opportunity existed; reputation bonus without trade activation; no contested resource pressure.

## Project code comparison

Compare Governing the Commons to Resource Island v1 outputs. The repo is strong where it reports activation pressure before interpreting institution effects.
